title: Own process and redirected handles explicitly
goal: Start and wait for a native child while retaining clear ownership of its process and standard handles.

selectionNotes: Own returned handles and keep redirected handles alive through startup. Do not mix Handle and Redirect flags. macOS execution is unverified.

constraints: Disposal closes a handle; it does not kill the process. Wait before disposing when completion is required. Open/TryOpen obtain separately owned handles; permission failures and exit/PID-reuse races remain possible after a successful lookup. The sample opens its current PID, disposes that independent handle and rejects a nonexistent PID with TryOpen. InheritedHandles selects native handles for inheritance; keep all entries alive until creation completes and do not share unrelated inheritable secrets. Console.OpenStandardInputHandle/OpenStandardOutputHandle/OpenStandardErrorHandle expose standard handles for native wiring; their returned wrappers and a child’s copies have separate lifetimes. Native launch callbacks are advanced alternatives: WindowsProcessStartArguments.Start expects a callback returning the created process handle; UnixProcessStartArguments.Start expects a PID. They provide prepared arguments/environment/standard handles, not an automatic OS launcher. No custom native callback implementation or callback execution is claimed by this example.
